payload.answer: It seems to me that you're not very critical here and do not capture the overall logic of plumb and how intent gets captured. Let's think what means an intent that is being merged. Word to intent matching should already have been validated locally when merged. So what's the point of having the words versionized? and then why should it be re-checked everytime?

options.description: The record is still judged and nothing is held, but it isn't fast-approved; it's judged again where your words are available.
options.label: Mark it, no fast path (Recommended)

options.description: A judgment without your words counts fully, with nothing marked.
options.label: Treat it like any other

payload.question: So on a machine without your private log: an intent record can't be checked against your words at all, and a requirement only against its intent record. Should those judgments be marked "made without your words" and kept from the fast approval path, so they get checked again on this machine?
